description: sc: at session start, name the SwarmCloud workflows and single tasks (in no workflow) that THIS Claude Code session started and that are still running -- each submission is tagged with the session id the hook reads on stdin, and other sessions' work in the same tenant, and untagged work, is never named -- so the session's first action is /sc attach --all; and, at session start only, the work still running for THIS project (whatever clones this checkout's origin repository, whichever session started it): in the rows layout it asks for /sc attach --all --project, in the pane layout the pane lists it once read. /sc check and the watch stay this session's. Read-only, silent when none run or anything fails; off when the plugin's auto_attach option is off. Claude Code has no hook event for /reload-plugins, so after a reload run /sc attach --all by hand. When work of yours is running and no watch was ever set for this project, it also asks the session to arm the /sc watch (CronList first, never a second job), unless /sc watch off was saved for the project. It also records the session id after /clear, so the plugin's MCP server tags and scopes by the session's current id. When /sc watch was turned on for this project (a preference saved under the bridge's config directory, read locally), it also asks the session to run /sc watch <N>m to re-arm the recurring /sc check, even with auto_attach off. It also loads ONE function-hooks module, ./pane.tsx: the SwarmCloud pane (`/sc-pane`, `/sc layout pane`), which reads SwarmCloud with one direct MCP call per click and never on a timer, so browsing costs no model tokens; at session start it makes ONE swarm_layout call and, in the pane layout, opens the pane unread (from 144 terminal columns, the engine's floor for an unasked pane); /sc layout rows|pane also re-attaches (/sc attach --all, one chat turn); in the band layout (/sc layout band) the same module draws the SwarmCloud levels in a strip above the prompt with a summary line below it, starts no /workflows rows, re-reads the list once a minute only while anything runs, and queues one /sc status chat turn when a workflow finishes or waits on a person, and at session start this script then asks for no attach; function hooks are early access, and where they are off the module does not load and everything else works as before.
